terms.gloss: edge, border; the kerb of a road
evidence: Liv. 41.27 (Lewis & Short s.v. marginō): roads to be edged, marginandae
terms.comment: The edge of anything (Lewis & Short); Livy speaks of roads to be edged, marginandae (41.27, cited by Lewis & Short s.v. marginō). Levi and Bini give margō viae for the pavement itself, and viam margināre for laying one. Masculine or feminine; written masculine here, as in edge.
Traupman gives the same phrase for the pavement (379); see pavement.

sources: Lewis & Short: margo · Lewis & Short: margino · Lewis & Short: crepido
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 299, 379.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 40.
